claims.text: The trip record establishes the two distances the threshold test runs on: the platform's optimal route for this booking was 14.0 km, and the vehicle actually covered 18.2 km, an excess of 4.2 km. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are met on the face of the record — 4.2 km is greater than 0.8 km absolute, and 30.0% is greater than 20% of the optimal distance.

POL-RD-01 requires the threshold test to be run on the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy, and here the two agree: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.2 km and trip_record.actual_distance_km is 18.2 km. The excess is therefore 4.2 km against the 14.0 km optimal, and the deviation is ESTABLISHED on the governing field.

The rider has carried the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-02849 and the same pickup window (requested 07:44:09, started 07:51:59), and the excess of 4.2 km / 30.0% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'Navigation rerouted me.' That is a general assertion of an external traffic cause, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the driver's burden. No advisory identifier is cited anywhere in the counterparty statement.

No traffic advisory covers this trip at all: the only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and has no payload, so the POL-RD-03 comparison — does an advisory name a road the optimal route traverses, with an overlapping validity window, matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor — cannot be run on this record. POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's traffic excuse carries no weight.

Under POL-RD-13(2) the consequence is arithmetic, not escalation: the rider has shown an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, the driver cited no advisory identifier, and the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact. The deviation stands at the measured 4.2 km and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked 14.0 km optimal route.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy. On the fare_breakdown constants — base 3.80, 0.75/km, 0.28/min, surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN, platform fee 0.80, no ERP, no surcharge, no promo — the recomputed fare for the 14.0 km / 19.0 min optimal route is 20.42, against a charged_total of 26.73. The rider is out of pocket on this trip: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the 26.73 stands against the rider and a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.35 is money actually returned, not a bookkeeping entry.

The chat log is empty — 0 messages, no waypoint_hint, no rider instruction of any kind — so POL-RD-04 cannot exonerate any part of the excess: there is no rider-requested detour on this record, and the driver's 'navigation rerouted me' explanation is not a rider instruction.

No pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply and the baseline remains the booked 14.0 km optimal route.

The chat log for this trip is empty — 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp. There is therefore no rider instruction recorded anywhere that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. The driver has not asserted a rider-requested detour, and the record would not support one if he had.
